cards.title: Cash flow

metrics.label: Operating cash flow · free cash flow (latest year)
FCF margin trend
metrics.note: Free cash flow as a share of revenue, first vs latest fiscal year: is the business becoming more or less cash-generative?

metrics.label: Stock pay ÷ revenue
metrics.note: Stock-based compensation ÷ revenue (latest fiscal year): a real cost paid in shares. It equals 10% of free cash flow.

metrics.label: FCF / net income (3 years combined)
metrics.note: Free cash flow ÷ net income from the statements, same years. Above ~0.9x means profits arrive as cash.

metrics.label: Cash kept by management
metrics.note: Over the 3 years to 2026: free cash flow $343.6B minus dividends $46.4B and buybacks net of shares issued $272.1B.

metrics.label: Why it keeps it: where the cash went
metrics.note: Change in debt and cash on the balance sheet over the same years; the rest is mostly acquisitions and investments.

metrics.label: Return on the money it keeps
metrics.note: Extra after-tax operating profit ÷ extra invested capital over 2021-2026 (10-K history; see Returns on new money), against a 9.0% required return.  Graded under Business performance.

metrics.label: Capex / operating cash flow
metrics.note: How much of the cash must be reinvested just to run and grow the business.

metrics.label: Capex ÷ depreciation (3-yr average)
metrics.note: Above ~1.5x the company is building new capacity; about 1x it is replacing what wears out; well below 1x it may be under-investing. Not good or bad on its own. Capex is only 1.9% of revenue here, so depreciation is mostly amortisation of past acquisitions and the ratio says little.

metrics.note: Graded under Valuation.

metrics.label: Gross margin
